# regionalpcs

`regionalpcs` summarizes DNA methylation within user-defined genomic regions
using regional principal components. It returns sample scores, CpG loadings,
variance fractions, and the number of retained components for each region.

## Installation

Install the Bioconductor release compatible with your R version:

```r
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("regionalpcs")
```

## Getting started

Supply a numeric matrix or data frame with uniquely named CpGs in rows and
samples in columns. The first two columns of the mapping table contain region
IDs and CpG IDs. Every mapped CpG must occur in the methylation input.

```r
library(regionalpcs)
res <- compute_regional_pcs(meth, region_map, pc_method = "gd")
res$regional_pcs       # retained regional PCs by samples
res$percent_variance   # fractions of within-region variance, not percentages
res$loadings           # CpG loadings for each region
res$info               # region, retained dimension, number of mapped CpGs
```

See the [vignette source](vignettes/regionalpcs.Rmd) for a runnable example,
genomic-region mapping, an optional array-data workflow, and interpretation.
For the version installed in R, use `browseVignettes("regionalpcs")`.

## Interpretation

The package uses centered, unscaled PCA and either Gavish--Donoho (`"gd"`) or
Marchenko--Pastur (`"mp"`) dimension selection through PCAtools. Both selection
methods receive a fixed noise variance of 1 and retain at least one component.
Input scale matters: beta values and M-values need not produce the same retained
dimension. A retained PC is a summary of variation, not evidence by itself of a
biological signal or disease association.

Report problems through [GitHub issues](https://github.com/tyeulalio/regionalpcs/issues).
